summary: Spec fidelity (brief F2/F4, spec 11.7 steps 2 and 3; scenario atip.inputorder.06): a document's fragment problem answers before malformed argv for most argv failures but not all, so two failures of the same kind answer in opposite orders. Real binary, 'finding close <argv> --input {"roundd":1}': '--round abc', '--disposition zz', '--seq 1 --seq 2', '--as zzz', 'x y' and '--json=1' answer INPUT_INVALID UNKNOWN_KEY /roundd (step 2 first, as the contract says), but '--bogus' answers USAGE --bogus and a missing option value ('--round' last) answers USAGE --round (step 3 first). Same on 0.34, so not a regression, but the brief takes both into step 3 ('mal-formed argv: an unknown option, a value of the wrong type') after the fragment. The test pins the wrong half: 06 asserts 'an unknown option answers first as well' only against a valid document (conflict), and the INPUT_INVALID-before-argv assertion uses a wrong-typed --round, never --bogus. Cause: the unknown-option and missing-value failures are met while the command line is lexed, before the document is read. Blast radius: only a call that has both an unknown option or valueless option and a bad document; L2.input-refusals does not add argv, so the checker does not probe it.
